summary: Build a governed catalog, glossary, and metadata workflow in 5 days. Learn practical methods for trusted data discovery and governance.
lede: Data catalog, metadata and business glossary management helps teams organize data assets, technical metadata, and approved business terms so people can find data, trust definitions, and apply consistent meaning. This course focuses on governed discovery, metadata classification, glossary stewardship, lineage tracing, and access-aware publishing to connect governance practice with day-to-day operations. You will practice structuring glossary terms, linking technical metadata to business language, designing stewardship workflows, setting classification rules, and defining ownership for data assets. The course also introduces automated metadata harvesting, column-level lineage, active metadata, and practical deliverables such as a glossary template, metadata standards checklist, and catalog curation workflow.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage data meaning, metadata, and governed discovery across business and technical teams. It suits people who must keep a catalog usable, a glossary credible, and metadata consistent across changing data environments. Data Governance Managers who oversee metadata operating models and stewardship controls. Metadata Analysts who maintain catalog structure and technical attribute definitions. Data Stewards who validate glossary terms and resolve definition conflicts. Data Architects who align system metadata with governed enterprise terminology. Business Intelligence Leads who rely on trusted definitions for reporting consistency. Data Catalog Administrators who configure asset classification and ownership workflows. Data Quality Managers who connect metadata rules to data usage controls. Enterprise Data Managers who coordinate glossary governance across domains. Data Product Owners who document trusted data assets for reuse and discovery. Analytics Governance Specialists who manage lineage, definitions, and catalog adoption.
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of data governance, data management, or BI operations, plus familiarity with how data assets are documented in your organization. No coding is required, but you should be comfortable reviewing metadata, business terms, and data ownership structures. If you already use a data catalog, glossary repository, or metadata platform, bring examples of your current templates, term lists, or stewardship workflows for practical application.
